problem: Find the global maximum of the function $f(x,y)=xy-x-y$ on the closed triangular region $D$ with vertices $(0,0),\,(2,0),\,(0,2).$
worked_solution:
Since $f(x,y)$ is continuous on the closed, bounded region $D,$ the function attains a global maximum and minimum on $D.$

To find the extreme values, we follow three steps.

**Step 1.** Find the critical points of $f$ inside the region. 

To determine the critical points, we solve ${f}^{′}=0.$ Computing the derivative gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}y-1,\,x-1\end{aligned}].
$$

The derivative exists at each point inside $D,$ and it equals zero when

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}y-1=0 \\ x-1=0\end{aligned}\,⟹\,{\begin{aligned}x=1 \\ y=1.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

This gives us a single point $(1,1).$ Since the point $(1,1)$ is not in the interior of $D$,  we do not yet include it in the list of candidates for extrema (it lies on the line $y=2-x,$ in the boundary of $D,$ so we will consider it in the next step).

**Step 2.**  Find the points on the boundary of $D$ that could give rise to extreme values. 

To find the points on the boundary that could give rise to extreme values, we parametrize each part of the boundary:

- The line connecting $(0,0)$ and $(2,0)$ can be parametrized as

$$
r=⟨t,0⟩,\,t\in (0,2).
$$

The values of $f$ on the boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(t,0) \\  & =(t)(0)-(t)-(0) \\  & =-t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the derivative of $F(t)$ is constant. So, $F(t)$ does not have critical points on the open interval $t\in (0,1).$

- The line connecting $(0,0)$ and $(0,2)$ can be parametrized as

$$
r=⟨0,t⟩,\,t\in (0,2).
$$

The values of $f$ on the boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(0,t) \\  & =(0)(t)-(0)-(t) \\  & =-t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the derivative of $F(t)$ is constant. So, $F(t)$ does not have critical points on the open interval $t\in (0,2).$

- The line connecting $(2,0)$ and $(0,2)$ can be parametrized as

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨2,0⟩+t(⟨0,2⟩-⟨2,0⟩) \\  & =⟨2,0⟩+t⟨-2,2⟩ \\  & =⟨2-2t,2t⟩,\,t\in (0,1).\end{aligned}
$$

The values of $f$ on the boundary are given by the function

$$
\begin{aligned}F(t) & =f(x(t),y(t)) \\  & =f(2-2t,2t) \\  & =(2-2t)(2t)-(2-2t)-(2t) \\  & =-4{t}^{2}+4t-2.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the critical points of $F(t)$ on the open interval $t\in (0,1),$ we solve the following equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{F}^{′}(t) & =0 \\ (-4{t}^{2}+4t-2)^{′} & =0 \\ -8t+4 & =0 \\ t & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This equation gives one solution. Evaluating the corresponding values of $x$ and $y$ on the boundary, we obtain the candidate point $(1,1).$

Also, we have to include the corner points of the region as candidates for extrema. So, in total we obtain four candidates:

$$
(0,0),\,(2,0),\,(0,2),\,(1,1)
$$

**Step 3.** Evaluate $f(x,y)$ at each of the candidate points, and compare their values. 

Evaluating $f(x,y)$ at each of the points mentioned above, we get the following: 

| $(x,y)$ | $(0,0)$ | $(2,0)$ | $(0,2)$ | $(1,1)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x,y)$ | $0$ | $-2$ | $-2$ | $-1$ |

Therefore, on the closed region $D,$ we have that 

- $f$ attains the global minimum of $-2$ at the points $(2,0),\,(0,2),$ and

- $f$ attains the global maximum of $0$ at the point $(0,0).$
